name: Houston Welding Academy LLC
summary: Hands-on welding courses in Pasadena, Texas, with day and night classes in structural, pipe and specialty welding.

financing.text: Tuition is paid out of pocket, with a private student loan or scholarship, or on a payment plan.

hero.eyebrow: Accredited trade school in Pasadena, TX
hero.title: Elevating welding
hero.lead: One of the most affordable accredited welding programs in the Houston area, with 100% hands-on training and no tools required to start.
hero.imageAlt: A gloved hand running an arc along a steel joint as sparks fly

groups.title: Structural Welding
groups.summary: Plate courses that prepare you for entry-level structural work in construction and industry.
groups.intro: Structural courses are built around carbon steel plate. You learn the arc process itself alongside welding and cutting safety, metal preparation, weld quality, weld symbols and detail drawings, and employment readiness. On completion a graduate should be able to start work as an entry-level structural welder in the construction or industrial field.
groups.imageAlt: A welder running a bead on flat steel at a bench, blue sparks around the arc

services.title: SMAW Plate
services.text: Shielded Metal Arc Welding on carbon steel plate, designed for the beginner welder or the welder with some experience preparing for structural or industrial work.
points: Oxyfuel, plasma arc and air carbon arc cutting

services.title: FCAW & GMAW Plate Combo
services.text: The flux core arc welding and gas metal arc welding processes on plate, including all three modes of transfer: short arc, pulse and spray arc.
points: Arc welding safety and proper technique

groups.title: Pipe Welding
groups.summary: Pipe courses in the 2G, 5G and 6G positions, taught to ASME welding code.
groups.intro: Pipe work is where the positions get harder and the money follows. These courses cover electrode and process selection, welding safety and proper technique for pipe in the 2G, 5G and 6G positions. The SMAW pipe course is taught to meet ASME welding code.
groups.imageAlt: A welder in a helmet striking an arc with a stick electrode on a length of round pipe

services.title: SMAW Pipe
services.text: Welding safety, proper technique and electrode selection for the Shielded Metal Arc Welding process on pipe in the 2G, 5G and 6G positions, to meet ASME welding code.

services.title: GTAW (TIG)
services.text: The gas tungsten arc welding process from arc welding safety through proper technique, metal preparation and weld quality.

services.title: FCAW & GMAW Pipe Combo
services.text: The flux core arc welding and gas metal arc welding processes on pipe, with short arc, pulse and spray arc transfer.
points: Cutting, metal preparation and weld quality

groups.title: Specialty Welding
groups.summary: Longer combination courses and stainless steel, for welders who want the widest range of work.
groups.intro: The combination courses put plate and pipe together in one program, so a graduate leaves with a certificate of completion and more than one process behind them. Plate and pipe welders can seek work at commercial construction companies, towers, nuclear energy plants, refineries, pipe yards and fabrication companies.
groups.imageAlt: A worker cutting steel tube with an oxyfuel torch, sparks pouring off the cut

services.title: Combination Welder
services.text: Plate SMAW, pipe SMAW and pipe GTAW in one course. Hands-on plate work in 2G, 3G and 4G, and pipe work in 2G, 5G and 6G.
points: Two manual arc processes, consumable and non-consumable electrode

services.title: Stainless Steel Welding
services.text: An introduction to welding on stainless steel: how the process works, its advantages and disadvantages, and the techniques that improve a weld.
points: Tools, cleaning and safe machine operation

services.title: Pipe Specialty Welder
services.text: The combination course plus stainless steel welding: plate SMAW, pipe SMAW, pipe GTAW and stainless in 2G, 5G and 6G.
points: Stainless welders can seek work at sanitary and petrochemical facilities

promo.title: 2 extra weeks free on the combo course.
promo.text: Mention this offer at the time of enrollment.

about.title: Hands-on training, start immediately.
text: HWA is a welding academy full of opportunities with one of the most affordable accredited welding programs in the Houston area. Our mission is that every student who gets certified by HWA is highly trained and field ready to fill any vacant job position in the welding industry.

Training is 100% hands on and no tools are required to start. Between flexible scheduling, personalized training and job placement assistance, the journey towards becoming a skilled welder begins here.
Classes run two shifts, Monday to Friday, at the shop on Preston Avenue in Pasadena. Hablamos español.
about.imageAlt: Red and blue welding screens hung along the booth row inside the Houston Welding Academy shop

values.title: Certified instructors
values.text: Certified welding instructors keep the teaching current with industry knowledge, practical skills and safety standards.

values.title: 1-on-1 training
values.text: One-to-one sessions, pre-test practice, pre-job testing and one to four hours in the booth.

values.title: Flexible scheduling
values.text: A day shift in the morning and a night shift in the evening, Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: How old do I have to be to enroll?
faqs.a: All students must be at least 17 to be considered or accepted for any course at HWA. Students under 18 must have parental or guardian consent to enroll.

faqs.q: Do I need a high school diploma?
faqs.a: A high school diploma or GED is needed. If you do not have one there is an on-site 4th grade assessment test. We encourage all students to finish high school.
Day shift runs Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 12 PM. Night shift runs Monday to Friday, 6 PM to 10 PM.

faqs.q: Do I need my own tools or gear?
faqs.a: No tools are required to start. Before your start date HWA highly recommends you have your proper PPE.
Start the online application, or book a tour of the academy and come see the booths first.

facts.heading: Course Tuition
facts.text: Prices as listed in the Houston Welding Academy course shop.
items: FCAW & GMAW Plate Combo, 120 hours / 6 weeks: $500 – $2,500
FCAW & GMAW Pipe Combo, 120 hours / 6 weeks: $500 – $2,500
Combination Welder, full course, 360 hours / 18 weeks: $500 – $7,500
Pipe Specialty Welder, full course plus stainless, 480 hours / 24 weeks: $500 – $10,000

facts.heading: Enrollment Requirements
items: At least 17 years of age; under 18 needs parental or guardian consent
High school diploma or GED, or an on-site 4th grade assessment test
Proper PPE is highly recommended before your start date

facts.heading: Paying for Tuition
items: Out of pocket by cash, check or money order
A private student loan or scholarship

facts.heading: Booth Rental
facts.text: Daily and weekly booth rentals for welders who want time on the machines. Call the academy for current rental options.

facts.heading: Hablamos Español
facts.text: Spanish is spoken at the academy, and the courses can be followed in Spanish.

facts.heading: One-on-One Training
items: One to four hours in the booth

facts.heading: Field Simulators
facts.text: Scaffold welding simulators let students master essential skills in a safe, controlled environment, bridging the gap between theory and real-world application.

facts.heading: Tour Times
facts.text: Day tours run 8 AM to 12 PM and night tours 6 PM to 9 PM, booked as a personal tour of the academy.

facts.heading: Refund And Cancellation Policy
items: A full refund for any student who cancels the enrollment contract within 72 hours of signing it

A full refund for any student who cancels within the first five scheduled class days, the trial enrollment period, except that the school may retain no more than $100 in administrative fees and the cost of items of extra expense necessary for the portion of the program attended
After the cancellation period, the minimum refund is the pro rata portion of tuition and fees for the hours remaining, and no refund is due once 75 percent or more of the charged hours are completed

A full refund of all tuition where an enrollee is not accepted, a course is discontinued, enrollment was procured through misrepresentation, or the student withdraws during the trial enrollment period

A student called to active military duty may choose a pro rata refund, a grade of incomplete marked withdrawn-military with the right to re-enroll, or a final grade where at least 90 percent of the coursework is complete
Books, tools and supplies are refunded separately, and no refund is made once those materials are purchased
Refunds are completed within 60 days after the effective date of termination

facts.heading: Student Records
items: HWA follows the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act of 1974, and student records are kept in locked cabinets and shredded when destroyed
Records are kept at least five years after graduation or the end of the class, and academic records are kept permanently
A graduate can obtain a copy of their academic records by contacting the school director
Education records can include class lists, grade rosters, student schedules, welding tests and NCCER documentation
A current or former student can inspect their records on written request, made available within 30 days
Transcripts are not issued to a student who is delinquent on school charges or behind on financial loan repayments
HWA does not recognize any previous education, training or experience

facts.heading: Student Complaints
facts.text: A student with a concern is encouraged to schedule a conference with the school director. A formal written complaint gets a written response by the 10th business day after it is received, and a student who is dissatisfied with the response can file with the Texas Workforce Commission, Career Schools and Colleges, Room 226T, 101 East 15th Street, Austin, Texas 78778-0001, (512) 936-3100.

facts.heading: Follow HWA
facts.text: The academy posts student work on Instagram at @houstonweldingacademy and on its Facebook page.
